articles.title: Twins open to trading one of their starting pitchers this offseason
articles.description: Twins starters Joe Ryan, Pablo López, Dean Kremer and Bailey Ober can all become free agents following the 2027 season, raising the likelihood one of them is dealt this winter.

articles.title: Twins owner Tom Pohlad vows to increase payroll, understands fans’ patience has ‘run out’
articles.description: The Twins fell short of their goals with a 77-85 record, putting added pressure on the organization to build a playoff-caliber roster for 2027.

articles.title: Twins’ Ryan Jeffers is headed for free agency. But he isn’t ruling out a return.
articles.description: The Twins are set to lose Ryan Jeffers, Josh Bell, A.J. Minter and Taylor Rogers to free agency, with Jeffers expected to draw plenty of interest.

articles.title: After rocky 2026 season, Twins find hope in late youth movement: ‘Next year, it’s on’
articles.description: The Twins flopped with a 21-30 record over the final two months of the season, but some of their top prospects showed they’re ready for the major league spotlight.

articles.title: Twins fire pitching coaches Pete Maki, Luis Ramirez after staff struggles again
articles.description: The Twins finished 25th in MLB with a 4.56 ERA after ranking among the bottom 10 in each of the past three seasons.

articles.title: Twins spoil Rangers’ playoff hopes in season finale as Target Field attendance hits 17-year low

articles.title: Twins can’t play spoilers again as Rangers keep playoff hopes alive with victory at Target Field
articles.description: Luke Keaschall looks to stay hot after a four-hit game Friday at Target Field. Meanwhile, Texas and Houston are battling down to the wire for the final American League playoff spot.

articles.description: Coming off the best season of his career, Larnach could be squeezed out of a crowded Twins outfield that is trending younger.

articles.title: RandBall: Could the Twins’ next matchup with the Yankees finally come on a more level playing field?
articles.description: The Twins are 49-130 against New York over the past 25 seasons, a run of misery shaped partly by a massive payroll gap. MLB’s next labor deal could change that equation.
